# Today on Hacker News

## AI/ML

The artificial intelligence and machine learning space dominated discussions today with several significant developments. **Liquid AI revealed their 8B-A1B MoE model trained on 38T tokens**, showcasing continued progress in efficient model architectures. The community also engaged with **Notes from the Mistral AI Now Summit**, sharing insights from recent industry gatherings. Hardware efficiency remained a hot topic with **Show HN: Tiny-vLLM**, a high-performance LLM inference engine built in C++ and CUDA. Meanwhile, **Shift will clean homes for free to train future robots** sparked conversation about AI training data collection methods. The discussion extended to industry concerns in **Is AI causing a repeat of frontend's lost decade?**, examining whether AI is displacing traditional development roles.

## Programming/Engineering

Backend and systems engineering discussions centered around practical database solutions with **SQLite is all you need for durable workflows**, proposing SQLite as a robust foundation for persistent workflows. Algorithmic innovation appeared in **Bijou64: A variable-length integer encoding**, introducing a new compression technique. Frontend developers engaged with **On Rendering Diffs**, exploring visualization challenges in code comparison tools. The community also debated **You can just say it**, a post by antirez that likely touches on communication and tooling philosophy.

## Hardware/Physical Computing

Hardware enthusiasts discussed the **Framework 12**, debating whether its price point justifies the modular laptop's appeal. 3D printing innovation continued with **Print with dozens of colors: Our new open-source ColorMix for PrusaSlicer**, expanding color capabilities in additive manufacturing. Network engineers shared **Free full BGP feed**, providing valuable routing data for IPv4 and IPv6 networks.

## Society/Economics

Broader discussions included **The dead economy theory**, which appears to be the most upvoted story at 624 points, suggesting economic anxiety resonated strongly. Policy developments emerged with **The California state assembly has passed the 'Protect Our Games Act'**, aiming to protect the gaming industry. Retro computing nostalgia surfaced in **Snowboard Kids 2 is 100% Decompiled**, celebrating the preservation of classic game code.
